To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dominant diesel vehicle fleet in Hong Kong was dominated by only 7 models, accounting for about 78% of all remote sensing records, which showed different NO emission levels and trends.
the NO emission trends of individual dominant diesel vehicle models varied greatly and were affected by the engine/vehicle technology and retrofit.
the diesel NO emission factors were stable or decreased for the dominant vehicle models in Hong Kong, except for two models, which showed a significant increase in 2005-2006.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the NO emission trends of the diesel vehicles, and the results provide a better understanding of NO emission control technologies for diesel vehicles in the real world and a reference for the future development of diesel emission standards.
the emission control of individual models and provides a reference for the future diesel emission regulations.
the recent emission trends of the most dominant diesel vehicle models, which can be used as a reference for the emission inventory and policy evaluation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diesel vehicle emission trends are model dependent.
the NO emission factor of diesel vehicles was stable during the period studied.
the diesel NO emissions in Hong Kong were stable or decreasing during 2006–2016, but the NO emission trends of individual vehicle models were not necessarily consistent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the remote sensing technology could help to evaluate and monitor the effectiveness of emission control technologies and regulations.
the NO emission factor of a specific vehicle model is a function of its engine size, fuel injection technology and the year of manufacture.

the remote sensing data were able to provide the detailed information on the NO emissions of the individual diesel vehicle models, which would be useful for the policy makers to develop more effective emission control strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
remote sensing studies should be detailed to the model level in order to better understand the emission trends.
the remote sensing data can be used to evaluate the emission performance of different vehicle models and thus provide a more detailed and accurate picture of the emission trends.

it is important to analyze the emissions of individual vehicle models in detail, rather than the fleet average, in order to better understand the effectiveness of emission standards and to develop more targeted control measures.
